summary: This standards-track document defines IS-IS extensions to support multicast forwarding using Bit Index Explicit Replication. They let routers advertise the information BIER needs.

eli5.summary: A group message that marks who needs a copy with a bit pattern. IS-IS spreads the information routers need to do this.

questions: what is the bier info sub-tlv
subtitle: The IS-IS advertisements that let routers set up Bit Index Explicit Replication multicast.

tldr.problem: BIER forwards multicast by a bitmask in each packet header, but every router needs to learn subdomains, bit positions and MPLS label ranges ahead of time.
tldr.mechanism: A new BIER Info sub-TLV, attached to a router's host prefix in IS-IS, carries the subdomain, BFR-id and algorithm fields, with an optional sub-sub-TLV for MPLS label ranges per BitString length.
tldr.outcome: IS-IS becomes the underlay that distributes BIER information. The RFC is updated by RFC 9272.

today: RFC 8401 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 9272. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: What This Extension Does
sections.content:
Bit Index Explicit Replication (BIER, RFC 8279) encodes all intended multicast receivers as a bitmask in the packet header. Each receiver is a unique bit. A router that gets such a packet forwards it according to the bit positions, along a precomputed tree for each bit.

This RFC extends IS-IS for IP (RFC 1195) to distribute the information BIER domains and subdomains need. It defines one new TLV that every router taking part in BIER signaling advertises. Only MPLS encapsulation (RFC 8296) is covered. Other encapsulations and the use of several at once are out of scope.
sections.eli5: To send one message to many people by ticking boxes, everyone must know their own box. IS-IS is the notice board where routers post that.

sections.title: Domains, Subdomains and Where Information Lives
sections.content:
An IS-IS-signaled BIER domain matches the scope of distribution of the BFR-prefixes that identify the Bit Forwarding Routers (BFRs). Inside it, BIER information is advertised for one or more subdomains, each identified by a subdomain-id (SD). Each subdomain is tied to exactly one IS-IS topology (MT), and local configuration decides which <MT,SD> pairs a router supports.

BIER information is attached to a new sub-TLV in the extended reachability TLVs and always describes a host prefix that is a node address of the advertising router. Otherwise the advertisement MUST be ignored. So the prefix length MUST be 32 for IPv4 or 128 for IPv6. If the Prefix Attributes Flags sub-TLV is present, the N flag MUST be set and the R flag MUST NOT be set. The BIER sub-TLVs MUST be kept when a prefix is leaked between levels.
sections.eli5: A subdomain is like a separate class list. Each list is attached to one router's own address, never to some other address.

sections.title: Consistency and Error Handling
sections.content:
A subdomain lives in one and only one topology, and all routers in the flooding scope MUST advertise the same subdomain in the same multi-topology. A router that receives a mismatching <MT,SD> pair MUST report a misconfiguration and ignore all BIER advertisements for the conflicting pair. The RFC notes this partitions the subdomain. For example, <0,0>, <0,1> and <2,2> are valid together, but <0,0>, <0,1> and <2,0> are not, and the <0,0> and <2,0> advertisements must be ignored.

A BFER or BFIR with a configured BFR-id advertises it; otherwise it advertises the Invalid BFR-id. A valid BFR-id MUST be unique within the flooding scope. If duplicates are detected for an <MT,SD>, all routers advertising the duplicate are treated as if they had no valid BFR-id, so they cannot act as BFER or BFIR there.

Receivers MUST support logging any advertisement that violates these constraints, and logging SHOULD be dampened. Because BIER information is expected to change rarely, implementations SHOULD also dampen updates if changes continue for more than a few seconds of burstiness, to avoid excess LSP updates.
sections.eli5: Everyone must use the same class list and nobody may share a box number. If two kids claim the same box, neither gets to use it until it is sorted out.

sections.title: The BIER Info Sub-TLV and MPLS Sub-sub-TLV
sections.content:
BIER information rides in TLVs 235, 237, 135 or 236. The BIER Info sub-TLV may appear multiple times in a prefix-reachability TLV, once for each subdomain supported in the associated topology. It holds a type, a length, three 1-octet fields (BAR, IPA, subdomain-id), a 2-octet BFR-id and optional sub-sub-TLVs. BAR is the BIER Algorithm and IPA is the IGP Algorithm, and both shape how underlay paths are calculated. Non-zero values are outside the scope of this document. A router that does not support them and receives them SHOULD treat the advertiser as unable to support BIER.

The BIER MPLS Encapsulation sub-sub-TLV (type 1, length 4) carries Max SI (1 octet), the 4-bit encoded BitString length BS Len and a 20-bit Label, the first label of a range. Each Set Identifier maps to one label, with the first label for SI=0, the next for SI=1, and so on. The sub-sub-TLV MUST be ignored if the label for the Max SI exceeds the 20-bit range.

Repeating a BitString length in the same BIER Info sub-TLV means the whole sub-TLV MUST be ignored. Label ranges across all of a BFR's sub-sub-TLVs MUST NOT overlap, otherwise the router is treated as advertising no BIER sub-TLVs. Labels MUST NOT use the reserved values of RFC 3032.
sections.eli5: Each router posts a card with its list number, its box number and which batch of mailboxes (labels) it uses. If the card is muddled, everyone ignores it.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA added value 32, named BIER Info, to the "Sub-TLVs for TLVs 135, 235, 236, and 237" registry. It also created the "Sub-sub-TLVs for BIER Info Sub-TLV" registry under Expert Review, with value 1 for BIER MPLS Encapsulation.

A "BIER Algorithms" registry was also created. Its policies are Standards Action for values 0 to 127, Specification Required for 128 to 239 and Experimental Use for 240 to 254. Value 0 means no BIER-specific algorithm is used and 255 is reserved.
sections.eli5: A public list was started so that each kind of note and each algorithm number is written down once and nobody reuses it.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
IS-IS security is covered by RFC 5304 and RFC 5310. The RFC explains that the denial-of-service risk of setting too many bits in a BIER packet cannot be caused by tampering with these IS-IS advertisements. The BFIR itself chooses which bits to set, and the IS-IS data only builds the forwarding tables that map each bit to next hops.

Each replica a BFR forwards carries fewer bits than the packet it received, an essential property of BIER forwarding. Further BIER-specific security discussion is in RFC 8279.
sections.eli5: Messing with the notice board cannot make the sender tick extra boxes, because the sender decides that by itself.

fields.name: Max SI
fields.desc: Maximum Set Identifier used for this BitString length.
